name: Spiaggia Grande & the Lower Town
tagline: The postcard heart at sea level
description: The iconic lower town where the pastel cascade meets the main beach and the majolica-domed Santa Maria Assunta church. Boutique-lined stepped lanes, beach clubs, ferry dock and the busiest restaurants cluster here, right in the center of the classic Positano view and its constant summer buzz.
bestFor: First-time visitors who want the iconic setting and easy beach and ferry access
pros: Right on the main beach and ferry dock
Steps from the church, shops and top restaurants
cons: Most crowded and expensive part of town
Constant foot traffic and noise in season

name: Upper Town toward Chiesa Nuova
tagline: Where the buses stop and the views open up
description: The higher reaches near the SITA bus stops and the Chiesa Nuova area, the practical gateway to and from the coast road. Quieter and slightly more local than the beachfront, with sweeping panoramas over the whole village, though everything below means a long stair descent and climb back.
bestFor: Travelers who value bus connections, value and big views over beach proximity
pros: Easy access to SITA buses along the coast
Broad views over the cascade to the sea
A bit quieter and better value
cons: Long, steep stairs down to the beach

name: Fornillo
description: A short cliffside walkway west of Spiaggia Grande leads to Fornillo, Positano's smaller, more relaxed beach. Fringed by low-key beach clubs, casual trattorias and a couple of watchtowers, it offers the same turquoise water with noticeably fewer crowds and a gentler, more local pace.
bestFor: Beachgoers who want the Positano setting with fewer crowds
pros: Scenic seaside path to the center
cons: Fewer amenities than the main beach
Still reached via steps and a walkway

name: Montepertuso & Nocelle (above the village)
tagline: Hillside hamlets on the Path of the Gods
description: High above Positano sit the tiny hamlets of Montepertuso and Nocelle, linked by the internal bus and hundreds of steps. Nocelle marks the trailhead of the famous Path of the Gods, offering peace, authenticity and jaw-dropping views, a quiet base for hikers happy to trade convenience for scenery.
bestFor: Hikers and quiet-seekers wanting nature and value above the crowds
pros: Direct access to the Path of the Gods
cons: Remote, with many stairs and bus dependence
Far from the beach and nightlife
